claim: Huguet et al. 2025 report a single-site UWB indoor-positioning study at Le Corbusier Hospital ED, Firminy, France (7 March–21 April 2022). The paper associates anonymized staff tags with eight staff-type labels: assistant nurses, triage nurses, intensive care unit (ICU) nurses, waiting room nurses, short-stay unit (SSU) nurses, managers, doctors, and on-duty doctors. These are staff labels, not activity-region names or patient/locomotion categories. Separately, a medical-expert panel divided this ED floor plan into subareas and associated activities: care coordination, informatics, transit, care preparation, management, stock, care, cleaning and stock, and other. Source-described examples are the triage nurse office, welcome desk and shift-change meeting room (care coordination); three computer-equipped rooms (informatics); storage rooms with a sink (cleaning/stock); and the critical care unit, treatment rooms and medical imaging unit (care). A large short-stay hospitalization-unit corridor is explicitly mixed Transit/Informatics/Care, where minor care and mobile-computer administration may occur. The source warns that transit-area position alone does not identify activity, and that single-site generalizability may be limited. For staff-label classification, successive same-tag observations separated by less than 30 minutes were grouped into sequences; a hexagonal grid covered the entire site floor plan, with tested hexagon diameters from 1 m to 3.5 m. Per-sequence time proportions in hexagons were features for a random-forest staff-type classifier; its reported best specification used 1.75 m hexagons and 51 selected features. This is a site-specific classification method, not a generic ED location catalogue or an accessible route graph. The separate hourly distance measure computes Euclidean (straight-line, as-the-crow-flies) displacements between coordinates from the same tag and aggregates the resulting distances per hour in metres. It is a source-specific measurement; it does not establish O/D trips, obstacle-constrained routes, route connectivity/choice, patient movement, or a coordinate transform. No source-reported geometry revision, map-matching rule, or transferability result to another ED is established in the bound text; these remain unknown.

This location/activity record does not concern tracked patients.
